memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Chronic kidney disease stage 3, glaucoma.
Patient is a 44‑year‑old male lab technician from Hennur, Bengaluru. He reports fatigue and occasional mild ankle swelling; eye discomfort noted. On exam: BP 138/86, mild peripheral edema, no jugular venous distension. Fundoscopy shows mild cupping optic discs. Spirometry not indicated. Asthma Control Test not applicable. Smoking status: never. Plan: start telmisartan 40 mg OD, dapagliflozin 10 mg OD, furosemide 20 mg OD, sodium bicarbonate 500 mg BD for CKD; timolol 0.5% eye drops BD, latanoprost 0.005% eye drops HS for glaucoma. Order baseline labs and eye assessment.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I’ve noticed my ankles swell a bit after long shifts at the lab, and my vision sometimes feels a little blurry in the evenings. I’m taking the medicines as prescribed but wonder if the eye drops are causing the blurriness.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Chronic kidney disease stage 3, glaucoma.
Patient reports increased ankle swelling and occasional blurry vision. Exam: BP 142/90, 2+ pitting edema to mid‑calf, JVP normal. Eye exam: IOP Right 24 mmHg, Left 23 mmHg; mild conjunctival redness. Spirometry not performed. Asthma Control Test not applicable. Smoking: never. Plan: increase furosemide to 40 mg OD, add latanoprost HS if not already (already prescribed), counsel on compliance, recheck labs in 6 weeks.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Eye exam (glaucoma work‑up): Visual field testing shows early paracentral scotoma in the right eye; left eye full. Optic disc photography reveals cup‑to‑disc ratio 0.6 right, 0.5 left. No retinal hemorrhages. Intraocular pressure on medication: Right 20 mmHg, Left 19 mmHg.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Refer to Dr. Kiran Rao, Glaucoma Specialist, Narayana Nethralaya, for progressive optic disc cupping despite maximal medical therapy. Request urgent visual field repeat and consideration of laser trabeculoplasty.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Ophthalmology review: IOP controlled on current drops; visual field stable. Recommend continuing medical therapy, schedule laser trabeculoplasty in 3 months if progression. No surgical intervention needed now.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Chronic kidney disease stage 3, glaucoma.
Patient reports stable ankle swelling, no new visual symptoms. Exam: BP 138/88, trace edema. Eye IOP Right 20 mmHg, Left 19 mmHg. Labs reviewed: creatinine 1.5, eGFR 50, Hb 12.8. Smoking: never. Plan: maintain current CKD and glaucoma meds, repeat labs in 3 months, reinforce low‑salt diet.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I’ve had a mild cough for the past week, no fever or shortness of breath. I’m wondering if I should get the flu vaccine and if any of my medicines could be causing the cough.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Chronic kidney disease stage 3, glaucoma.
Patient reports mild non‑productive cough, no dyspnea. Exam: BP 140/90, lungs clear, no edema. Eye IOP stable. Labs: creatinine 1.5, eGFR 48, Hb 12.9. Smoking: never. Asthma Control Test not applicable. Plan: hold NSAIDs, give inactivated flu vaccine today, monitor cough; consider low‑dose spironolactone if edema worsens.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Appointment booked for 2026-04-10 09:30 with Dr Suresh Menon (Pulmonology) for routine CKD and glaucoma review. Patient confirmed via clinic app.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Chronic kidney disease stage 3, glaucoma.
Patient reports cough resolved after vaccine, no new symptoms. Exam: BP 136/84, lungs clear, no edema. Eye IOP Right 20 mmHg, Left 19 mmHg. Labs from 2025-12-10 reviewed; stable. Plan: add spironolactone 12.5 mg OD, reduce furosemide to 20 mg OD to limit electrolyte loss, continue telmisartan, dapagliflozin, sodium bicarbonate, glaucoma drops. Repeat labs and eye review in 4 months.
